children: Smiths Group reported a resilient performance against a challenging backdrop including the Middle East conflict, J.P. Morgan analysts say. The U.K. engineering company guides for 4% organic growth in fiscal 2027, broadly in line with consensus expectations, the analysts add. There are also positive developments beyond the numbers in the report, JPM says. These include the launch of a process to sell the John Crane U.S. legacy asbestos liability, which the analysts say would provide a free cash flow gain of 20 million pounds ($26.7 million). Smiths Group also reports higher exposure to data centers, tailwinds from greater energy security needs and portfolio development in the Flex-Tek business. This should allow the company to reach its medium-term growth target more quickly, the analysts say. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)
